extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated entities, attorneys, agency staff, and researchers who need to read or navigate Title 49 of the Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and structural information for locating, using, and giving feedback on the online Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR) for Title 49 (Transportation). Includes statements about legal status, navigation tools, feedback channels, and site features such as a drafting site and subscriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: eCFR legal status
rubrics_metrics.description: The Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR) is a continuously updated online version of the CFR; it is not an official legal edition of the CFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should "Learn more about the eCFR, its status, and the editorial process." Treat the eCFR as a convenient, up-to-date reference but verify legal requirements against the official published CFR when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official published CFR citation/source
rubrics_metrics.description: The most recent official publication of the CFR is available via the published edition on govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The official, published CFR is updated annually and "may not include the most recent changes applied to the CFR"; use govinfo.gov for the formal printed/legal version rather than relying solely on the eCFR for official citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content feedback procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you would like to comment on the current content, use the 'Content Feedback' button for instructions on contacting the issuing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For questions about the agency that issued a document, contact the issuing agency directly. Use 'Content Feedback' specifically for content corrections or comments; use 'Website Feedback' for site-related issues or suggestions to improve ecfr.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of the Federal Register (OFR) role disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of the Federal Register publishes documents on behalf of Federal agencies but does not have any authority over their programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When content-related authority is needed, "we recommend you directly contact the agency associated with the content in question." OFR/website staff can assist with site issues but not substantive agency program authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported browser requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The website is designed for the current versions of Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, or Safari.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users on unsupported browsers will see a message 'You are using an unsupported browser.' For full functionality and correct display, use one of the supported browsers listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting site availability for amendatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: A drafting site is available for use when drafting amendatory language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page provides an option to 'switch to drafting site' for users preparing amendatory text — use that environment when composing proposed regulatory amendatory language rather than the standard public view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigation/search guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Navigate the eCFR by entering citations or phrases (e.g., '1 CFR 1.1', '49 CFR 172.101') and by choosing items from citations, headings, or full-text search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing an item from citations and headings will bring you directly to the content; choosing an item from full text search results will bring you to those results. Pressing enter in the search box will also bring you to search results. Background and more details are available in the 'Search & Navigation' guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-in-time and subscription features
rubrics_metrics.description: The eCFR provides a Point-in-Time system and subscription options to access Title 49 as of specific dates and to receive updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page offers 'Using the eCFR Point-in-Time System', a 'Timeline' and 'Go to Date' features, and a subscription mechanism ('Subscribe to: Title 49 of the CFR') so users can view historical versions and follow recent changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization of Title 49 (parts, chapters, subtitles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title 49 is organized into subtitles, chapters, parts, and sections (e.g., Subtitle A: Office of the Secretary of Transportation; Parts 1–99; Chapters I–XII corresponding to agencies). The page lists part ranges and chapter headings for Title 49.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed part ranges and chapter mappings (e.g., Chapter I: Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration, Parts 100–199; Chapter V: NHTSA, Parts 500–599) to locate relevant regulatory provisions. The listing serves as an index to the structure of Title 49.
